also: go back the way we came

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation: deponent in the present, active in the perfect
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 3.31: exeuntem illum domō et revertentem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The writers before Augustus say revertor in the present and revertī, active, in the perfect, with the participle reversus; reversus sum comes later (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: ita maestus rediit, ut retractus, nōn reversus vidērētur
phrases.english: he came back so downcast that he seemed dragged back, not returned
I got it wrong: go back to the arcade

phrases.latin: Per angiportum rūrsum tē ad mē recipitō illāc per hortum.
phrases.english: Come back to me along the alley, that way, through the garden.
Let’s go back home; it’s getting dark.

phrases.latin: nihil optābilius esse quam redīre, quā vēnerant, sī possent
phrases.english: there was nothing they wished for more than to go back the way they had come, if they could

phrases.latin: salūtātīs dīmissīsque iīs eādem quā vēnerat viā … rediit
phrases.english: he greeted them, sent them off, and went back by the same road he had come
Let’s go back the way we came.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 218.
